question: Who is called fish-eater and who are called living-being-harmers?
premises: matsyāśī saḥ bhaved identifies the fish-eater
śeṣāḥ syuḥ prāṇihiṃsakāḥ describes the rest
inference: the verse distinguishes the fish-eater from the rest, who are living-being-harmers
uncertainties: whether bhaved and syuḥ are both optative or one conditional
plain_english: He would be the fish-eater, O goddess; the rest would be living-being-harmers.
